sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Eighty-seven-year-old Maricarmen Abascal died in hospital two weeks after being removed on a stretcher from her Madrid home of over seven decades. The flat's owner had significantly raised her rent, which exceeded her pension. Although the firm later offered a return agreement, Abascal died before signing. sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Abascal became a national symbol of the housing crisis. Tens of thousands protested, setting up encampments in Madrid and other cities. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for discovering chemical reactions that produce large excesses of one chiral form of a molecule. Kagan showed that a chiral catalyst could drive reactions favoring a single chirality. Soai found reactions where a product acted as a catalyst to boost the same reaction, turning a tiny initial excess into over 99 percent of a single form.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Life relies on molecules with specific handedness, or chirality, and key enzymes fail to work with the wrong form. Finding new ways to catalyze specific chiral forms helps address challenges in origin-of-life research. It also has immense practical utility for producing pharmaceuticals, as wrong chiral forms in drugs can be inactive or harmful.
